title: Cost of the ticked three-query test
statement: Let $n\in\mathbb{N}$, let $f:\{\pm1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$ be a Boolean function, and let $x,y\in\mathbb{F}_2^n$. Running the three-query BLR program after charging $2n+1$ local computation steps has probability-one outcome equal to true exactly when $F(x)+F(y)=F(x+y)$, where $F$ is the binary encoding of $f$; its cost is $(0,3,2n+1+3)$ (random examples, queries, and local work, respectively).
hypotheses_covered: Boolean target function on the sign cube
